title: Make task-key allocation collision-safe at creation time
description:
## Summary
The 2026-09-11 audit window contains a live MemorySmith task-key collision wave. Keys `TSK-0197` through `TSK-0205` each carry 2–3 distinct active records that share one key (19 records over 9 keys), produced by at least three independent sessions allocating keys concurrently. `TSK-0189` made `Scripts/Normalize-TaskRecords.ps1` collision-safe when *repairing* drift, but nothing guards *creation-time* allocation. Separately, the create/update API accepted a record whose `externalLinks` shape its own reader rejects, leaving `TSK-0206` (`hasLoadError: true`) unreadable.

## User Mandate
> "Synthesize the latest unreviewed audits and re-review the other recent audits from the last 2 days or so in order to extract all relevant information into the task system, or to improve the agent/skills/process/development pipeline aspects"

STRICT. Do not narrow or re-scope this requirement; surface any proposed change first.

## Scope
- Make task-key allocation collision-safe at creation time: scan every existing `Data/Tasks/*.json` id/key before assigning the next key, and fail or reassign on collision.
- Repair the live collision wave through a supported MemorySmith path (no hand-editing `Data/Tasks/*.json`): preserve every distinct mechanism under a unique key, naming replacements.
- Harden the record schema so create/update rejects shapes the reader cannot load (for example `externalLinks` supplied as strings instead of link objects).
- Keep the normalizer's fail-closed behavior and `TSK-0189`'s collision-safe repair path intact.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Creating a task never produces a second live record with an existing key.
- The live collision census (`TSK-0197`..`TSK-0205`) is resolved to one canonical record per key, with superseded/renamed records archived and naming their replacement.
- `TSK-0206` loads without `hasLoadError`, or its record is replaced by a loadable canonical record.
- `Scripts/Normalize-TaskRecords.ps1` and the repository task-record validator report no duplicate keys.

## Validation
`memorysmith_task_list` census showing unique active keys; `memorysmith_task_get` for every previously colliding key; `Scripts/Normalize-TaskRecords.ps1` read/write-safe run; repository task-record validation; `git diff --check`.

## Findings
Source-confirmed 2026-09-11 via live MemorySmith responses. Duplicate keys observed: `TSK-0197` (2), `TSK-0198` (2), `TSK-0199` (2), `TSK-0200` (3), `TSK-0201` (2), `TSK-0202` (2), `TSK-0203` (2), `TSK-0204` (2), `TSK-0205` (2). `TSK-0206` returns `hasLoadError` because `externalLinks[0]` is a string, not a `TaskExternalLink` object. Root cause is creation-time allocation across independent sessions, not the normalizer.

## Blockers
The MemorySmith tool surface exposes no key-rename operation; resolving the wave may require an API/repair-path change recorded here rather than ad-hoc record deletion.

## Next Step
Add the creation-time uniqueness preflight, then reconcile the live collision wave and verify the census.

comments.body: Validator evidence (2026-09-11 synthesis). `Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` still fails: it reports every key in the `TSK-0195`..`TSK-0205` collision wave as duplicate, plus the historical `TSK-0153`/`TSK-0188`/`TSK-0189` pairs and missing-field schema errors in older records. Archiving a duplicate live record (`set_status` = Archived) does NOT clear the validator: it counts archived JSON files as duplicates. So the acceptance criterion requires either (a) the validator to exclude `isArchived` records, or (b) a supported rename/delete path for the colliding `Data/Tasks/*.json` files. This is a validator/tooling gap to add to this task's scope.

comments.body:
Real-world collision evidence (2026-09-11). Two distinct records currently share key `TSK-0198`:
- `tsk-0198-stream-preview-generation-hotpaths-and-direct-edge-ownership` (Performance; reporter ChatGPT; the stream-preview/extraction perf slice)
- `tsk-0198-define-portable-animation-clip-and-sampling-contract` (Task; animation clip/sampling contract)

Impact observed: `task_add_comment` called with `idOrKey: "TSK-0198"` was mis-routed to the animation task. The bare key is not sufficient to identify the record; callers must pass the full slug id. This also means any key-based lookup, status change, or handoff reference to `TSK-0198` is ambiguous.

Requested behaviour: make key allocation collision-safe at creation time (refuse or disambiguate), and make key-based resolution fail loudly on ambiguity instead of silently choosing one record. Suggested validation: a test that creates a second record whose normalized key collides and asserts creation fails (or produces a distinct key), plus a resolution test that asserts an ambiguous key returns an error rather than a record.
